fields.title: Autonomy and Control - Mission Quiz
fields.description: Five questions covering the same topics on every attempt. Pass with at least three correct.

fields.title: A Claim Was Not Control Everywhere
fields.content:
A colonial authority could claim a territory without controlling every community within it. To investigate actual control, ask what happened in a particular place and period. Were instructions carried out? Was tribute collected? Who made decisions? A boundary drawn on a map does not answer all these questions. A single expedition also does not automatically establish lasting rule.

Our fictional source desk compares a map claim, an order and a record of a local action. The map shows what its maker represented. The order shows what an authority wanted. The action record may help investigate practice. Keep their dates and purposes separate. Do not turn one successful visit into permanent control of a whole region, or one failed action into proof that no contact ever occurred. This is a way to read evidence, not a map of present-day legal rights or instructions about modern government.

fields.title: Autonomy Meant Local Decisions
fields.content:
Communities could maintain important decisions and institutions beyond effective Spanish rule. In this historical lesson, autonomy concerns local affairs and authority. It does not mean that everyone in a community had equal power, that no rules existed, or that the community had no connections with others. Ask which decisions people maintained and under what conditions.

A UCLA research summary of Stephen Acabado and Marlon Martins work describes Ifugao resistance to Spanish conquest alongside strategies for strengthening local organization. This is a named case, not every highland communitys identical history. Our modern clue card asks who made a decision and what evidence shows it being carried out. It is not a drawing of a universal council or a present-day legal definition of autonomous regions. More detailed Ifugao and other Cordillera histories follow later in the chapter.

fields.title: Contact Did Not Automatically Mean Conquest
fields.content:
Communities could trade, negotiate or encounter colonial forces without every interaction producing complete colonial control. A treaty text records an agreement or claim, but its implementation needs evidence. A garrison is a military post; its presence in one place does not by itself establish identical authority throughout surrounding communities.

Najeeb Saleebys 1908 History of Sulu distinguishes Spanish claims and positions from limits on authority beyond them. The book also collects treaty texts and accounts of trade. Read it critically: it was written after Spanish rule in an American colonial setting and contains dated language and judgments. We use a limited example to ask about different forms of authority, not to repeat its stereotypes or decide present-day territorial disputes. A fuller account of Muslim polities and communities follows in Mission 2.

fields.title: Autonomy Did Not Mean an Unchanging Life
fields.content:
Resisting conquest did not require a community to remain unchanged. People could adjust livelihoods, organization and relationships while defending local authority. Terrain could affect movement and resources, but mountains alone do not explain peoples decisions or every colonial outcome. Keep the people and their actions in the explanation.

The UCLA account of Ifugao research describes people using economic opportunities and strengthening local organization. This challenges a picture of an isolated society frozen outside history. Our fictional comparison cards show a community keeping a local decision while changing an exchange activity. They illustrate a possible relationship, not a surviving transaction or proof of every persons motive. To explain actual change, use archaeological, documentary and community evidence for the named place and period. Change is not a measure of greater or lesser human worth.

fields.title: Compare Claims with Community Evidence
fields.content:
A colonial report might call an area controlled while local evidence points to different limits. Do not assume that one official label is the complete story. Ask who produced each source, when, for what purpose and whose actions it records. Community knowledge and archaeological evidence can help investigate questions that an official report leaves out.

UCLA describes collaboration between researchers and descendant communities in interpreting Ifugao history. This is not permission to invent a single voice for every community member. Our fictional portfolio separates a map claim, a dated action record and a later community account. Match each to a question it can support, and identify gaps or disagreement. A modern account should keep its own date rather than be presented as an unchanged colonial statement. No student is asked to disclose ancestry, faith or family identity to complete the activity.

fields.title: Prepare Your Autonomy Evidence Report
fields.content:
Review five ideas. A territorial claim was not proof of effective control everywhere. Autonomy concerned local decisions, not the absence of institutions. Trade, treaties and military posts required separate evidence about actual authority. Communities could change and interact while defending local affairs. Different sources and community knowledge help investigate limits.

Prepare a fictional report for another Grade 5 learner. Name the people, place and period, explain the claim or recorded action, give a supporting clue and state a limit. Do not use one garrison as every communitys experience, mountains as the only explanation, or resistance as proof of complete isolation. Label the source cards as models, and keep historical questions separate from present-day legal claims.

The main quiz has five questions and three correct passes. Review linked learning content before practice and a retry if needed. Only Chapter 11 Mission 1 is ready in this release. Completing it does not finish the chapter or award its final badge: Missions 2-4 and the chapter challenge are still being prepared.
